propositions: Test runs 884 renderable units through serial pandoc spawns (~1768 total) in a single monolithic loop, causing unbounded per-test cost: 91.6s idle, 504.8s under CPU saturation, exceeding CI's 300s per-test timeout guard on the contended macOS lane.

pytest-timeout with thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the xdist worker process outright without traceback or assertion text, manifesting as 'node down: Not properly terminated' followed by worker crash in CI reports.

Test cost is load-dependent and corpus-size dependent; the monolithic structure means growing the corpus lengthens a single case rather than adding cases, preventing structural closure of the failure mode.

Fix chunks the equivalence test with fixed-size batches (40 units per chunk) parametrized by chunk index, distributing work across xdist workers and bounding per-test cost independent of load and corpus growth.
New coverage guard test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit asserts chunk concatenation equals the full unit list and total >= 100, ensuring no units are silently dropped by chunking.
All 884 units remain compared with real pandoc on both sides at stride 1; byte-identity property is untouched; no timeout raise, retry marker, or elapsed-time assertion is added.
